LESSON: TRANSPOSITION

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: MUSIC AND DANCE FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Foundations of Music and Dance
Topic 1.3: Transposition
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 11

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Transposition, part of Foundations of Music and Dance in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 MUSIC AND DANCE FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: How does transposition aid in music performance?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Transposition together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication: The learner clearly and effectively discusses with peers the process of transposing music to a given

interval, an octave or a given key.

● Collaboration: The learner shares information with others while transposing melodies an octave up or down within the

same or to a different stave.

● Creativity and imagination: The learner comes up with new musical ideas when singing or playing melodies at different

pitches higher or lower to distinguish the difference in pitch.

● Critical thinking and problem solving: the learner reflects and assesses a variety of alternative musical ideas when

transposing melodies to a given key within the same or to a different stave.

● Learning to learn: The learner applies compositional skills and knowledge on digital software to compose and transpose

music an octave higher.

● Digital literacy: The learner uses music notation software to write music an octave higher or lower.

11

Values:
● Respect: The learner displays humility as they recognize input of every member when giving and receiving feedback on

transposing melodies an octave higher or lower.

● Unity: The learner discusses transposition processes with others to create new melodies.

● Responsibility: The learner uses digital equipment with assistive technology and materials responsibly.

● Love: The learner shares learning resources with others when creating transposing melodies an octave higher or lower.

● Peace: The learner avoids conflict as they give constructive feedback on others’ compositions.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Life skills: The learner uses techniques learnt in music transposing melodies to grow talent.

● Cyber security: The learner uses digital apps responsibly.

● Self-esteem: The learner believes in themselves as upcoming artistes as they acquire knowledge on transposing melodies

an octave higher or lower.

Suggested Learning Resources

Digital devices with appropriate assistive technology, Sheet music in appropriate print and in music braille notation, Braille

equipment and materials, Textbooks in appropriate print and in braille format, Music Braille Code, 2015

Manuscripts books in appropriate print, melodic instrument, piano keyboard

Suggested Key Skills Assessed

● Describing intervals in major keys.

● Explaining transposition.

● Transposing a melody to a given interval.

● Transposing a melody from treble to bass.

● Transposing a melody from bass to treble.
